summary: The first section states who created the project and includes a text about NASA and space; the second section features photographs taken in space; the third section contains a photo of a rocket that was abandoned in space and later brought back to Earth; the fourth section provides information about NASA; the fifth section highlights an astronaut from NASA who traveled to the Moon; and the sixth section includes a farewell note, the names of the creators, and the sources from which the information was gathered.
details: This project gives information about abandoned vehicles and space junk in space. It explains how broken satellites and rocket pieces are moved to "graveyard orbits" or brought back to Earth to ocean graveyards like Point Nemo.It raises awareness about the dangers of space trash. It helps people understand crash risks in space and how this affects both space and Earth's oceansIt aims to educate young people and the public about the challenges of space exploration. It specifically points out the dangers of uncontrolled space junk and the risk of Kessler Syndrome.The project was made using presentation software, and the information and pictures were collected from online sources like Google, Reddit, Pinterest, and NASA.It brings together real-world topics—like how orbits work, graveyard orbits, and dropping space junk into the ocean—into an interesting presentation format made for young peopleThe team thought about safety risks in space (like Kessler Syndrome), high-speed crash dangers for active satellites and astronauts, and how to safely bring spacecraft down into faraway parts of the ocean.
